dedupe_keys.name: bredbandskollen swedish crowdsourced internet speed measurements with half yearly statistics and table annex

description: Bredbandskollen is an independent consumer tool run by the Swedish Internet Foundation, the registry for the .se and .nu domains, for measuring internet speed through a web browser, mobile apps, a command-line client and an Apple TV app. Each test sends data over websockets for 10 seconds in each direction to the nearest of four measurement nodes in Sundsvall, Stockholm, Gothenburg and Malmö, with servers also serving Norway and Denmark, and rates the result against the subscribed speed. The statistics page reports on the measurements: in the first half of 2026 more than 11 million tests were made, of which about 4.5 million carry GPS information placing them in Sweden and form the basis of the statistics. Results include average download and upload speeds for the web tool each year from 2008 (12 and 5 Mbit/s) to the first half of 2026 (181 and 152 Mbit/s), speeds by county inside and outside built-up areas (on average 193 against 121 Mbit/s), and breakdowns by device, mobile network and wifi and 2G to 5G technology, with each chart exportable as CSV, XLSX or JSON and a table annex workbook for the half year. The site also offers a speed map (Surfkarta). Coverage: Sweden, with some tests in Norway and Denmark. Format and access: web statistics with CSV, XLSX and JSON chart exports and an XLSX annex, free. Caveats: crowdsourced tests depend on who measures and on home wifi; individual measurements are not published; licence terms for reuse were not stated on the page read. Simulation uses: county and urban-rural speed baselines for service models, and long-term growth in delivered speeds. Related records: the Nordic-Baltic telecom statistics and Danish telecom statistics give provider-reported figures, and Breitbandmessung and RTR-NetTest are comparable measurement tools.
